summary: Several studies have applied transformer models to credit card fraud detection with varying success. Okafor et al. (2023) [D0042] used self-attention sequence models on the SentinelYield-2 dataset, achieving an accuracy of 0.89. Novak et al. (2018) [D0044] also employed self-attention sequence models but on the OpenGrid-5 dataset, reporting an accuracy of 0.901. Zhou et al. (2018) [D0048] explored decentralised model updates for fraud detection on the SentinelYield-2 dataset, obtaining a MAPE of 0.805. Although not directly on credit card fraud, Lindqvist et al. (2024) [D0052] and Okafor et al. (2020) [D0054] mentioned prior work on the topic, indicating its relevance and application in similar financial detection tasks.
